subject: Request: SLA carve-out for tool-invocation + structured-output failures (CloudNova)
messages:
From: Jordan Reed <jordan@cloudnova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: cloudnova-support@cloudnova.com
Date: 2027-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Intermittent structured-output failures impacting order extraction

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a spike in structured-output parsing failures from your hosted endpoint yesterday evening (around 18:30 UTC). The failures are triggered when our tool-calls to our external inventory service return 504 or partial JSON fragments — Redwood's response ends up as malformed structured output which our downstream pipeline rejects.

This is causing retries and backpressure in our ingest, and the client (an enterprise retail customer) is flagging SLA breaches on our side. Our contract expects 99.95% availability for text-generation and 50ms p50 latency for single-turn tool-invocations; we need to understand whether these tool-call induced failures are eligible for an SLA carve-out under Redwood's policy, and if not, request a temporary exception while we implement mitigation.

Can you confirm:
- Is Redwood treating tool-invocation timeouts / external webhook failures as part of the SLA window?
- If not, what evidence/format do you need for an exemption?
- Any recommended immediate mitigations we should apply (retry/backoff config, fallback models, structured-output validation)?

I've attached execution traces and sample failing payloads. Happy to jump on a quick call this afternoon.

Thanks,
Jordan Reed
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudNova

Attachment stubs: execution_trace_20271114.zip (log archive), sample_payloads.json (examples)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reed <jordan@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent structured-output failures impacting order extraction

Jordan — thanks for the details and the traces. We're looking into the traces now. Short answers first:

- By default our hosted SLA covers the end-to-end response from Redwood's API (including time spent waiting for tool-calls that originate inside the Redwood runtime). For cases where the tool-call reaches an external third-party service that we do not control (your inventory webhook), we do have an operational carve-out path but it requires evidence and a mitigation plan.

- To consider an exception we need: request timeline, frequency of incidents, representative logs (you provided), and a proposed mitigation + rollback plan.

Immediate mitigations we recommend:
- Configure Redwood client-side retries with exponential backoff (we can suggest client SDK values).
- Use structured-output validation with a graceful fallback (e.g., return best-effort JSON along with a warning field) so your pipeline can accept and repair in-flight.
- If possible, decouple non-critical tool-calls via async batching (reduces p99 latency impact).

I've looped Dev (SRE) and Marcus (Product) to prepare an internal impact assessment and a formal carve-out request that we can sign off with legal/ops. Can you share a short list of times when you observed the failures and an estimate of how many user-facing requests were affected?

—Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success (SaaS)
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-15T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: assessment for CloudNova carve-out request

Team — I reproduced the scenario in staging by forcing timeouts on outbound tool-invocations. Observations:

- When the tool-call returns 504 or truncated bodies, the runtime attempts a single retry (default). The downstream structured-output serializer can fail if partial tokens are returned, leading to a 500-level response to the customer.
- These failures are intermittent and correlate with elevated latency to the customer webhook between 18:10–19:00 UTC on 2027-11-13 and again on 2027-11-14.
- Impact measured on CloudNova's traces: ~0.4% error rate for affected routes during the spike window; estimated 2,900 user requests impacted (their estimate).

Proposed carve-out terms (draft):
- Exclusion window: failures attributable to external webhook timeouts and truncated payloads, when evidence shows external service responded with 5xx or timed-out, are carved out from the uptime SLA for a defined remediation window.
- Temporary credit: For incidents we put into the carve-out bucket, offer a one-time service credit (0.25% of monthly invoice) as goodwill during the 30-day remediation period.
- Mitigation obligations: Customer must implement recommended retries + structured-output validation within 14 days; Redwood will provide a runtime toggle to increase client-side retry attempts and a recommended fallback behavior.

Attachments: summarized traces attached for legal/ops review. I recommend Marcus shepherd the external communication.

—Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: execution_trace_20271114.zip
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reed <jordan@cloudnova.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-16T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carve-out for tool-invocation + structured-output failures (CloudNova)

Jordan — thanks for your patience. Legal and Product reviewed the draft and we're prepared to move forward with a formal carve-out and remediation plan. Summary of agreed items:

1) Carve-out scope: tool-invocation failures caused by downstream external webhooks (HTTP 5xx, timeouts, truncated payloads) where evidence shows the error originated outside Redwood. These incidents will be excluded from SLA uptime calculations for the impacted routes during the remediation window.

2) Customer obligations: CloudNova will implement the structured-output validation and the recommended retry/backoff configuration within 14 calendar days and share a verification run (sample logs + synthetic traffic) for Redwood to confirm.

3) Remediation timeline & credit: While the customer completes remediation, Redwood will apply a temporary goodwill credit equal to 0.25% of the monthly invoice for the current billing cycle, applied after a post-mortem is accepted.

4) Operational controls: Redwood will provide a toggle to enable a more conservative retry policy at the route level and a diagnostic flag that appends webhook latency metadata to our request logs for easier attribution.

Next steps:
- Jordan: share the exact incident times and a quick verification script (we'll accept the sample synthetic test you used).
- Kimberly: I'll draft the carve-out amendment and loop Legal for signature (DocuSign link included).
- Dev: please prepare the diagnostic toggle and a one-off log export for the 18:10–19:00 UTC windows.

I'll attach the draft amendment for review. If that's acceptable, we'll route for signature and put the exemption into effect once verification is complete.

Thanks — Marcus
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
